kicker: A bonsai reads a whole library, gets pruned, and only then learns to answer.
summary: AI guesses from what it has learned — let it look things up, and check for yourself.

quiz.q: AI gives an important number with total confidence. What should you do?
options: Trust it — it sounds so sure
Check it against a trusted source
Ask the exact same question again
Ignore it, AI always gets numbers wrong
quiz.explain: AI can make things up very confidently; for anything important, open the source or cross-check one more place.

life.label: A tree’s life
life.art: Ink painting: a young tree on a rock in a sand garden. A cloud of words rains down from above and the tree grows fast and wild; then it is pruned to a scroll of principles; finally the tree answers a question.
life.holdAria: Hold to rain words onto the tree (or hold the space bar)

steps.label: Read
steps.aria: Step 1: pre-training — reading a mountain of text

life.question: “Write me a New Year wish”
life.askAria: Ask the tree: write me a New Year wish
life.answer: “Peace, prosperity, and may all your wishes come true!”

insights.text: Pre-training: AI reads a huge pile of text to learn to guess the next word — it knows a lot, but grows wild.
insights.detail: For example: books, web pages, code… Afterwards it continues text very well but doesn’t yet behave like an assistant.

insights.text: Fine-tuning: people score answers and write principles, pruning it into a more helpful, safer assistant.

detail.text: For example: Anthropic trains Claude with a “constitution” (Constitutional AI) that explains how to behave and why.

insights.text: Answering (inference): the shaped tree simply answers with what it learned — it doesn’t grow while you chat.
insights.detail: To teach it something new, you retrain it, or put documents right into the question — like the lookup scene ahead.

think.label: Scratch paper
think.art: A still life on a low wooden table: a small sheet for answering right away, a large scratch sheet for writing step by step. Beside each sheet sit an incense burner (time) and a dish of pebbles (tokens).
think.question: A pen and an eraser cost $11. The pen costs $10 more than the eraser. How much is the eraser?
think.fastAria: Let the AI answer right away
think.slowAria: Let the AI work it out step by step, then answer
think.insight: Thinking mode: AI drafts step by step before answering — more tokens and time, but fewer mistakes on hard problems.

detail.text: Models that “think” before answering appeared in 2024. Easy tasks don’t need it switched on — it only costs more.

hallu.label: The cracked stone
hallu.art: A stream with three stepping stones, each carrying one claim from the AI’s answer. One is a fake stone the AI placed where it didn’t know; tap it and it cracks and sinks.
hallu.question: Q: Who made ChatGPT, and when did it launch?

stones.aria: Test the claim: ChatGPT was made by OpenAI
Test the claim: launched in March 2021
Test the claim: built on GPT models

hallu.insight: AI can make things up very confidently to fill gaps — this is called “hallucination”. For anything important, verify.
hallu.detail: Good habit: ask for sources, open them and read, cross-check one more place — especially numbers, names and dates.

rag.label: The lookup lantern
rag.art: A stone lantern (the AI’s memory) and a small library across the gravel path. The AI can answer right away, or bring documents back to the lantern first and then answer.
rag.question: Q: How long is our company’s Lunar New Year break?
rag.memoryAria: Let the AI answer from what it already remembers
rag.lookupAria: Let the AI search the company documents, then answer
rag.guessNote: a guess based on what’s typical
rag.answer: 9 days off, from the 27th of the 12th lunar month.
rag.insight: Lookup (RAG): AI finds relevant documents, puts them into its context, then answers — with a source you can check.
rag.detail: Web search works the same way: AI reads a few fresh pages before answering. Its built-in memory may be outdated or incomplete.

pond.label: One pond, three streams
pond.art: Three streams — text, images, sound — flow into one pond, like a single model that can read many kinds of data. At the bottom of the pond, a mist still lingers.
pond.diveAria: Look down to the bottom of the pond
pond.insight: Multimodal AI reads text, images and sound in one single model — three streams, one pond.
pond.detail: For example: snap a photo of a bill and say “split it evenly between 4 people” — AI reads the photo, hears you, and does the math.
pond.deep: AI is superb at spotting patterns, but it doesn’t “understand” the way people do. What goes on inside models is still being researched.
pond.deepDetail: Scientists are “peering” inside models — this is called interpretability — but much is still unclear.

openai-chatgpt.title: Introducing ChatGPT
openai-chatgpt.note: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT on November 30, 2022, fine-tuned from a model in the GPT-3.5 series.
